Fun Soulslike with deep buildcrafting and solid core gameplay, puzzles, loot, and tons of secrets.

Pros:
- Boss design is usually good, sometimes great, and always varied. Every boss fight has something unique to separate it from the others without feeling gimmicky
- Gunplay and melee combat is satisfying
- Tons of secrets and puzzles to discover
- Loot always feels meaningful and unique (you never go from a level 10 blue shotgun to a level 11 purple shotgun)
- Secrets and randomized levels give each world a decent amount of replay-ability.  You won't be able to get every piece of loot or fight every boss on a single playthrough
- Deep buildcrafting with multiple playstyles (glass cannon, tank, healer, pets/summoning, status effects, etc.) to mix and match as you earn more loot

Cons:
- When playing co-op, netcode can be poor, especially at high ping. Very noticeable when trying to use non-hitscan weapons (bows, grenade launchers). Also no ping/connection quality indicator when joining public lobbies, and frequent random disconnects when trying to join one
- Overall short campaign (first playthrough took 12 hours with mostly full-clearing every area, now I can blow through a fresh campaign in under 5 hours)
- Getting good performance heavily relies on supersampling/DLSS

It's a really fun game to play with friends, but it's far from a masterpiece.

The worlds are quite unique, and it's very interesting to explore them and find all the events and secrets. Each world has different mechanics and two different 'biomes', so they feel different. The aesthetic is quite different between them too.

(Un)fortunately, you can't get all the events and secrets in one run. So you need to reroll the adventure until you get them. That's one of the key premises of the game, the procedural generation, but I don't think it works. On paper, the procedural generation would add a lot of replayability to the game, but because of the way it was designed in this game, it just adds boredom.

Each world has some 'dungeon' levels that are connected to some 'overwold' levels (that connect to several dungeons). Most of the interesting content happens in those 'dungeon' levels, but in order to get there, you have to find them in the overworld. And when you've played the overworld of one map, repeating it is pointless, as they are very similar between rerolls.

The same happens with the dungeons: when you've played one of them once, repeating it is boring. However, if you want to get all the secrets, you have to replay the dungeons too, as sometimes you miss one secret. Or even worse: the dungeon didn't 'generate' the secret, so you need to reroll the adventure, hoping that you get that dungeon, and hoping that the dungeon generated the secret that you wanted.

So, essentially, the procedural generation just makes accessing the content more difficult to artificially increase the playing time. I think the game would be much better if you could get all the events in one run, instead of this chore. Or, even better, if the procedurally generated content would be more different.

Apart from that, the story itself is not very interesting, and it ends with some kind of cliffhanger that I assume will be resolved on future DLCs. I really hate games that don't properly end the story until a DLC, but the story of this one is not that important to begin with, so it's not that bad. The lore of each world is quite interesting though, and there's a lot (especially in Yaesha). They usually lore dump you a lot of information though.

There are lots of weapons and equipment. That's good and bad, as you have lots of options to create your build, but it's also a bit overwhelming, as there's no UI to filter it. I confess that I've ignored the relic fragments completely lol, as it was too much. I haven't needed them for now (I've played the first and second difficulty setting).

The archetypes are a really great addition to the game, as they have very different playstyles. I feel that the level up is too slow (I guess this is another way to artificially increase the playing time), so you need quite some time to get the most of each archetype. Also, the items to unlock some of them are very hidden, and sometimes the game doesn't give you a hint (as far as I know). One or two of them are impossible to get without a guide. I like games with secrets, but it's a bit pointless that the only way to get some of them for most of the players is to use a guide.

In conclusion, a fun game to play with friends. It’s sometimes repetitive, as you need to reroll adventures to get all the content, but it’s not that boring in multiplayer.
